decision_evidence: Interactive owner instruction on 2026-08-17 (Claude session 8e2f9bb1-b00a-4d9f-9a42-74b1d318c22b): asked 'how to create a score file' for QS-C21; offered (A) an independent open-source pipeline run outside QualSight in its own virtual environment or (B) a third-party/vendor file; owner replied verbatim: 'option a'.

Option A as executed: insightface 0.7.3 FaceAnalysis(name='buffalo_l', det_size=640) — insightface's own detection, alignment, face selection (highest det_score), and w600k_r50 recognition model — run from ~/venvs/extscore over the 6,000 frozen LFW View 2 pairs (pairs.csv exported from the recorded protocol), writing external_scores.csv and a provenance sidecar with model file hashes.

Honesty note: the artifact is genuinely computed outside QualSight's frozen matcher runtime (different software stack and recognition model), but it is not a foreign vendor file; the plan records it as INDEPENDENT_OPEN_SOURCE_PIPELINE evidence, weaker than a genuinely third-party artifact. The buffalo_l detector file coincides byte-for-byte with QualSight's registered SCRFD-10G model; the recognition model and pipeline code differ.

Third-party rights note: insightface buffalo_l models are released for non-commercial research use; the artifact is derived biometric data over the LFW funneled release and stays local; redistribution is not allowed.
permitted_actions: Register the score table and its provenance sidecar as an EXTERNAL_SCORE_ARTIFACT resource with pinned hashes.
Import it through the QS-C21 importer over the frozen protocol, marked EXTERNALLY_COMPUTED, and evaluate it with the registered verification definitions.
Run the beta terminal gate QS-H74 with this artifact as the external-score step of the section-57 chain.
prohibited_actions: Do not present the artifact as a vendor or third-party result.
Do not redistribute the score table or bundle it with QualSight.
Do not re-score it inside QualSight or alter its rows to fit the protocol; unmapped rows are refused.
